# What does this PR do ?

This PR moves MoE perf recipes on GB200 and VRNVL72 from the HybridEP flex dispatcher to NCCL EP, with `moe_use_grouped_tensor=True`. It follows #6171 (GB300) and #6261 (GPT-OSS 120B GB200 MXFP8). The VRNVL72 switch is there to measure NCCL EP's impact on that platform.

# Changelog

Every switched recipe calls `_enable_ncclep` and sets `moe_use_grouped_tensor=True`. Its inline environment sets `NCCL_EP_HT_EM_PULL_PUSH=1` in place of the HybridEP topology names. `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0` stays on the DeepSeek recipes. Parallelism, precision, recompute, CUDA graph mode and comm overlap are unchanged.

## GB200: 10 recipes

| Family | Recipes |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek V3, 256 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, MXFP8 large-scale |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash, 128 GPUs | MXFP8 |
| Nemotron 3 Super, 64 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, 8 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8 |

## VRNVL72: 27 recipes

| Family | Recipes |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek V3 | 128 and 256 GPUs: BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4. 64-GPU and 4-GPU proxies: MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash, 128 GPUs | MXFP8 |
| GPT-OSS 120B, 64 GPUs | MXFP8 |
| Nemotron 3 Super, 64 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, 8 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8 |
| Qwen3 235B-A22B, 256 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Qwen3 30B-A3B, 8 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Qwen3.5-VL | 35B on 8 GPUs and 397B on 64 GPUs: BF16, MXFP8 |

## GB300: 1 proxy

`deepseek_v3_pretrain_64gpu_gb300_fp8mx_proxy_config` now builds on the 256-GPU GB300 MXFP8 parent, which already runs NCCL EP with grouped tensors, and swaps its HybridEP environment for `NCCL_EP_HT_EM_PULL_PUSH=1`. #6603 requires this proxy to stay identical to the 64-GPU VRNVL72 MXFP8 proxy, which this PR moves to NCCL EP. It has not been benchmarked on NCCL EP.

# Results

NCCL EP runs come from this branch and HybridEP runs from `main`. Each pair ran the same nemo-ci test on the same image (`nightly-2026-10-16`, same digest). TFLOP/s/GPU is the mean over steps 31–45 (the CI window); memory is peak reserved per GPU. † BF16 recipes also turn on `moe_use_grouped_tensor`, so their deltas are not dispatcher-only. Full report with kernel breakdowns: https://claude.ai/artifact/DViKpKB3u5fkAZ4WFr8v1L

**VRNVL72, 128–256 GPUs**

| Benchmark | Parallelism | HybridEP | NCCL EP | Δ | Peak mem (GB) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DeepSeek V3 BF16 † | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 1610.0 | 1632.7 | +1.4% | 192.7 → 193.5 |
| DeepSeek V3 MXFP8 | PP2 VP8 EP32 | 2887.1 | 2948.6 | +2.1% | 256.7 → 243.6 |
| Qwen3 235B NVFP4 | PP4 VP12 EP32 | 2134.2 | 2205.7 | +3.3% | 244.2 → 235.6 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP8, 128 GPUs | EP32 | 1215.1 | 1243.5 | +2.3% | 268.7 → 266.9 |

- Same-image HybridEP reruns for Qwen3 235B BF16 (NCCL EP 1389.2) and MXFP8 (NCCL EP 2210.8) are still queued. DeepSeek V3 NVFP4 has no NCCL EP number: its run hit the 1-h Slurm limit before finishing model and optimizer setup.

**VRNVL72, 8–64 GPUs**

| Benchmark | Parallelism | HybridEP | NCCL EP | Δ | Peak mem (GB) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GPT-OSS 120B MXFP8 | EP16 | 1570.3 | 1603.3 | +2.1% | 186.9 → 185.9 |
| Nemotron 3 Super MXFP8 | EP8 | 1491.8 | 1595.9 | +7.0% | 280.4 → 272.4 |
| Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4 | EP16 | 1264.2 | 1447.3 | +14.5% | 276.1 → 273.9 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning BF16 † | EP8 | 1167.7 | 1284.6 | +10.0% | 220.5 → 220.7 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning MXFP8 | EP8 | 1261.0 | 1402.4 | +11.2% | 258.2 → 257.3 |
| Qwen3 30B-A3B BF16 † | EP8 | 1047.7 | 1316.1 | +25.6% | 264.4 → 267.6 |
| Qwen3 30B-A3B MXFP8 | EP8 | 1521.4 | 1609.5 | +5.8% | 178.5 → 176.5 |
| Qwen3.5-VL 35B BF16 † | EP8 | 708.9 | 848.3 | +19.7% | 221.5 → 223.8 |
| Qwen3.5-VL 397B BF16 † | EP32 | 864.0 | 912.0 | +5.6% | 268.9 → 270.5 |
| Qwen3.5-VL 397B MXFP8 | EP32 | 1133.2 | 1210.9 | +6.9% | 251.8 → 255.2 |

- A/A control: GPT-OSS 120B BF16 on `alltoall` in both pipelines differs by −0.4%.

**GB200**

| Benchmark | Parallelism | HybridEP | NCCL EP | Δ | Peak mem (GB) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DeepSeek V3 BF16 †, 256 GPUs | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 885.6 | 905.7 | +2.3% | 161.8 → 163.0 |
| DeepSeek V3 MXFP8, 256 GPUs | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 1265.0 | 1306.9 | +3.3% | 172.8 → 171.3 |
| DeepSeek V3 NVFP4, 256 GPUs | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 1481.9 | 1492.6 | +0.7% | 185.9 → 185.9 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP8, 128 GPUs | EP32 | 733.4 | 750.3 | +2.3% | 184.1 → 183.2 |
| Nemotron 3 Super MXFP8, 64 GPUs | TP2 EP16 | 761.6 | 780.1 | +2.4% | 160.2 → 160.2 |
| Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4, 64 GPUs | TP2 EP16 | 701.1 | 723.3 | +3.2% | 171.5 → 171.1 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning BF16 †, 8 GPUs | EP8 | 785.5 | 823.2 | +4.8% | 168.2 → 172.7 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning MXFP8, 8 GPUs | EP8 | 852.5 | 891.7 | +4.6% | 154.4 → 154.3 |

- In every EP ≤ 32 pair in the tables above, NCCL EP spends less GPU time per dispatch+combine and exposes less communication. Overlapping compute kernels run longer, which gives back part of the saving.
- At EP64 (DeepSeek V3) the gains are smaller. On VRNVL72 BF16, NCCL EP's dispatch+combine takes 25% longer (1,652 vs 1,327 µs) and the gain comes from the grouped-tensor GEMMs. On GB200, every DeepSeek V3 HybridEP run slows by 1.4–2.4% between steps 11–20 and 31–45 while NCCL EP does not, so over steps 11–20 the DeepSeek V3 gains are only +0.2% to +1.1%.
- Peak reserved memory changes by −13.1 to +4.5 GB per GPU. The largest increase on GB200 is +4.5 GB (Lightning BF16).

## Tests

- The new `test_gb200_ncclep_perf_recipes.py` checks the full NCCL EP stack on 12 GB200 recipes (this PR's 10 plus the two Nemotron 3 Ultra recipes from `main`). It also checks that 14 GB200 recipes kept on HybridEP don't pick it up: the four Qwen3 235B-A22B 256-GPU recipes this PR no longer switches, and 10 others, several of which share a base or parent recipe with a switched one.
- `test_gb300_ncclep_perf_recipes.py` now checks the NCCL EP stack on all 29 VRNVL72 NCCL EP recipes: the 27 above plus the two Nemotron 3 Ultra recipes. This replaces its check that the VRNVL72 aliases stay on HybridEP. It also checks that the 16 VRNVL72 MoE recipes left off NCCL EP don't pick it up.
- Existing tests that hardcoded HybridEP for switched recipes are updated:
  - GB200:
    - The Nemotron 3 Super BF16 perf-vs-library test now treats NCCL EP as a benchmark-only difference. The library recipe stays on HybridEP.
    - The Lightning-vs-Nano policy test allows for the dispatcher environment differing between the two.
    - The DeepSeek V4 Flash GB300 test also asserts that GB300 stays on HybridEP.
  - VRNVL72: the full-iteration, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V3 proxy and Qwen3.5-VL workload tests now expect NCCL EP.
  - GB300: the DeepSeek V3 MXFP8 proxy parity test now expects NCCL EP on both 64-GPU proxies.

# Scope

- **GB200:**
  - When this PR was opened, nemo-ci benchmarked 22 GB200 MoE recipes, all on HybridEP. `main` has since moved Nemotron 3 Ultra MXFP8 and NVFP4 to NCCL EP, and this PR switches 10 more.
  - DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP8 is switched without GB300 precedent; #6171 removed its GB300 switch as unverified.
  - Left on HybridEP, although their GB300 counterparts run NCCL EP: Kimi K2 MXFP8, Nemotron 3 Nano BF16/MXFP8, and Qwen3 30B-A3B 8-GPU BF16/MXFP8 and 32-GPU BF16.
  - Qwen3 235B-A22B 256-GPU BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 and MXFP8 large-scale also stay on HybridEP: NCCL EP showed no gain (see [Validation](#validation)). Their GB300 counterparts run NCCL EP.
  - GPT-OSS 120B BF16 stays on `alltoall`, as on GB300.
  - GB200 recipes without a nemo-ci benchmark are not touched.
  - `deepseek_v3_pretrain_256gpu_gb200_fp8mx_partial_cg_dev_config` stays on HybridEP deliberately: it offloads `expert_fc1` with EP overlap, and MCore rejects that combination under `ncclep`.
- **VRNVL72:**
  - Only the tracked benchmarks switch; the rest stay identical to `main`.
  - Some switched recipes have no NCCL EP counterpart on GB200 or GB300: Qwen3 30B-A3B NVFP4, Qwen3.5-VL 35B MXFP8, and Qwen3.5-VL 397B BF16 and MXFP8.
  - DeepSeek V4 Flash ran on NCCL EP on GB200 and VRNVL72 with `nightly-2026-10-16` ([Results](#results)). An earlier GB200 NCCL EP run hit the determinism error below.
  - SM budgets come from the HybridEP recipes. Megatron-Core routes `moe_hybridep_num_sms` to `moe_flex_dispatcher_num_sms`, which NCCL EP uses: 32 SMs for most recipes and 16 for Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.

# DeepSeek determinism setting

- In nemo-ci, DeepSeek V4 Flash GB200 on NCCL EP failed in the first backward pass with TE's `Deterministic execution was requested (NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0 …), but the scale gradient (dprob) is accumulated with nondeterministic atomics` error.
- **Correction to an earlier version of this description: the error is not specific to NCCL EP.**
  - TE raises it in the op-fuser fused grouped MLP (`ops/fused/grouped_mlp.py`) for routed experts whenever `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0` is set and the cuDNN frontend has no deterministic dactivation.
  - Megatron-Core passes the routing probabilities into that MLP the same way for HybridEP and NCCL EP.
  - The check arrived with TE #3407 (2026-09-04), so the recipe's HybridEP golden most likely ran on an older container.
- Any DeepSeek recipe that uses the op fuser and pins `=0` can therefore hit this error on a recent container, whatever its dispatcher. That includes `main`'s GB200 HybridEP DeepSeek V3 MXFP8/NVFP4 recipes. On `main`, the GB300 DeepSeek V3 recipes no longer pin the setting, apart from the dedicated deterministic recipe.
- **This PR keeps `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO` as on `main`: `=0` on the GB200 and VRNVL72 DeepSeek recipes, and `=1` on the GB300 and VRNVL72 64-GPU MXFP8 proxies (#6603)**, so the dispatcher stays the only difference from the HybridEP baselines.
- On a container where TE raises this error, the DeepSeek recipes that use the op-fuser grouped MLP fail in the first backward pass on either dispatcher:
  - GB200: DeepSeek V3 MXFP8, NVFP4 and MXFP8 large-scale, and DeepSeek V4 Flash.
  - VRNVL72: DeepSeek V3 128-GPU MXFP8, 256-GPU MXFP8 and NVFP4, the 64-GPU NVFP4 and 4-GPU MXFP8/NVFP4 proxies, and DeepSeek V4 Flash.
- On VRNVL72, the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning recipe notes that the Rubin image lacks TE #3273 (2026-08-31), which would put it before this check. That is unverified.

# Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- Local CPU unit tests were run with CPU torch and Megatron-Core at `main`'s pin `3914483`, using import-only stubs for Triton and TE.
  - The GB200 and GB300/VRNVL72 NCCL EP tests pass 97/97.
  - Across 23 related test files, 1255 passed and 38 failed:
    - 37 need Hugging Face config downloads, which are blocked locally.
    - `test_known_cross_package_collisions_have_explicit_benchmark_precedence` fails the same way on a clean `main` snapshot.
  - `tests/unit_tests/scripts/performance/test_recipe_environment.py` could not run locally (no `nemo_run`). This PR does not change launcher code.
  - The functional test `test_perf_config_integration.py` was updated but could not run locally, because it also needs HF configs.
- After merging `main` (7623dab, conflict with #6567 in `test_nemotron_3_5_lightning_perf_recipes.py`): `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass and pre-commit passes. The unit tests were not rerun locally after the merges: the local test environment has transformers 4.57, and this branch requires 5.15 or later. GitHub CI runs them.
- The 29 VRNVL72 NCCL EP recipes build offline and pass Megatron-Core's NCCL EP constraints:
  - none uses drop-and-pad;
  - the static-capacity recipes have the op fuser, grouped GEMM and `NVTE_CUTEDSL_FUSED_GROUPED_MLP=1`;
  - none combines A2A overlap with `expert_fc1` offload.
  - Rubin reports compute capability 10.7, which Bridge's NCCL EP hardware check accepts.
- nemo-ci benchmark results are in [Results](#results). These runs used the container's Megatron-LM, not Bridge's pin.
- **Dropped from this PR after measurement on NCCL EP:**
  - GPT-OSS 120B BF16 measured 543.6 vs 581 TFLOP/s/GPU (−6.3%) against its `alltoall` golden.
  - GPT-OSS 120B BF16 on VRNVL72 (switched in 86df0e8, reverted in f61f7da) measured 776.6 vs 887.2 TFLOP/s/GPU (−12.5%) against an `alltoall` run on the same image. NCCL EP passes FP32 routing probabilities, so GPT-OSS's expert-bias add runs in FP32 (+366 ms per iteration); the dispatcher kernels themselves take less GPU time than `alltoall`'s.
  - Qwen3 30B-A3B 8-GPU measured +2.4% (BF16) and +1.9% (MXFP8).
  - Qwen3 235B-A22B on 256 GB200 GPUs measured 793.6 vs 797.0 TFLOP/s/GPU (−0.4%, BF16), 1097.6 vs 1097.2 (+0.0%, MXFP8) and 1217.2 vs 1227.7 (−0.9%, NVFP4) against same-image HybridEP runs. Its MXFP8 large-scale recipe, which builds on the MXFP8 recipe, was not measured and stays on HybridEP too.

# Before your PR is "Ready for review"

**Pre checks**:

- [x] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests?
- [ ] Did you add or update any necessary documentation?
- [ ] Does the PR affect components that are optional to install? (Ex: Numba, Pynini, Apex etc)
  - [ ] Reviewer: Does the PR have correct import guards for all optional libraries?

**Still to do:**

- [ ] Finish the VRNVL72 comparison. Done for 14 benchmarks ([Results](#results)). Same-image HybridEP reruns for Qwen3 235B BF16/MXFP8 are queued; DeepSeek V3 256-GPU NVFP4 needs an NCCL EP rerun. Loss was not compared.
- [x] Rerun the 64–256-GPU GB200 benchmarks and compare them against HybridEP ([Results](#results); Qwen3 235B-A22B under [Validation](#validation)).
  - GB200 has much less HBM than GB300, where NCCL EP added up to about 13 GB of device memory for Nemotron 3 Super. On GB200, peak reserved memory rose by at most 4.5 GB.
  - The llmb scale-out jobs reuse these base recipes.
- [x] DeepSeek V4 Flash on GB200 ran on `nightly-2026-10-16` (+2.3%).
- [ ] Refresh the nemo-ci goldens afterwards, starting with Lightning BF16 on GB200. Re-check the `KNOWN_ISSUE` flags (MB-1707, MB-1203) and `allow_failure` on DeepSeek V4 Flash.
- [ ] Model verification cards still record the earlier HybridEP measurements for some of these recipes. Refresh them once new numbers exist.
- [ ] Expect conflicts with #6372 in `perf_recipes/deepseek/gb200/deepseek_v3.py`, and in `perf_recipes/deepseek/vrnvl72/deepseek_v3.py` once #6372 follows the `vr200` to `vrnvl72` rename.

# Additional Information

- Follows #6171 and #6261.

detail.body:
# What does this PR do ?

This PR moves MoE perf recipes on GB200 and VRNVL72 from the HybridEP flex dispatcher to NCCL EP, with `moe_use_grouped_tensor=True`. It follows #6171 (GB300) and #6261 (GPT-OSS 120B GB200 MXFP8). The VRNVL72 switch is there to measure NCCL EP's impact on that platform.

# Changelog

Every switched recipe calls `_enable_ncclep` and sets `moe_use_grouped_tensor=True`. Its inline environment sets `NCCL_EP_HT_EM_PULL_PUSH=1` in place of the HybridEP topology names. `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0` stays on the DeepSeek recipes. Parallelism, precision, recompute, CUDA graph mode and comm overlap are unchanged.

## GB200: 10 recipes

| Family | Recipes |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek V3, 256 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, MXFP8 large-scale |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash, 128 GPUs | MXFP8 |
| Nemotron 3 Super, 64 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, 8 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8 |

## VRNVL72: 27 recipes

| Family | Recipes |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek V3 | 128 and 256 GPUs: BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4. 64-GPU and 4-GPU proxies: MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash, 128 GPUs | MXFP8 |
| GPT-OSS 120B, 64 GPUs | MXFP8 |
| Nemotron 3 Super, 64 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, 8 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8 |
| Qwen3 235B-A22B, 256 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Qwen3 30B-A3B, 8 GPUs | BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 |
| Qwen3.5-VL | 35B on 8 GPUs and 397B on 64 GPUs: BF16, MXFP8 |

## GB300: 1 proxy

`deepseek_v3_pretrain_64gpu_gb300_fp8mx_proxy_config` now builds on the 256-GPU GB300 MXFP8 parent, which already runs NCCL EP with grouped tensors, and swaps its HybridEP environment for `NCCL_EP_HT_EM_PULL_PUSH=1`. #6603 requires this proxy to stay identical to the 64-GPU VRNVL72 MXFP8 proxy, which this PR moves to NCCL EP. It has not been benchmarked on NCCL EP.

# Results

NCCL EP runs come from this branch and HybridEP runs from `main`. Each pair ran the same nemo-ci test on the same image (`nightly-2026-10-16`, same digest). TFLOP/s/GPU is the mean over steps 31–45 (the CI window); memory is peak reserved per GPU. † BF16 recipes also turn on `moe_use_grouped_tensor`, so their deltas are not dispatcher-only. Full report with kernel breakdowns: https://claude.ai/artifact/DViKpKB3u5fkAZ4WFr8v1L

**VRNVL72, 128–256 GPUs**

| Benchmark | Parallelism | HybridEP | NCCL EP | Δ | Peak mem (GB) |

| DeepSeek V3 BF16 † | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 1610.0 | 1632.7 | +1.4% | 192.7 → 193.5 |
| DeepSeek V3 MXFP8 | PP2 VP8 EP32 | 2887.1 | 2948.6 | +2.1% | 256.7 → 243.6 |

| DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP8, 128 GPUs | EP32 | 1215.1 | 1243.5 | +2.3% | 268.7 → 266.9 |

- Same-image HybridEP reruns for Qwen3 235B BF16 (NCCL EP 1389.2) and MXFP8 (NCCL EP 2210.8) are still queued. DeepSeek V3 NVFP4 has no NCCL EP number: its run hit the 1-h Slurm limit before finishing model and optimizer setup.

**VRNVL72, 8–64 GPUs**

| Benchmark | Parallelism | HybridEP | NCCL EP | Δ | Peak mem (GB) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GPT-OSS 120B MXFP8 | EP16 | 1570.3 | 1603.3 | +2.1% | 186.9 → 185.9 |
| Nemotron 3 Super MXFP8 | EP8 | 1491.8 | 1595.9 | +7.0% | 280.4 → 272.4 |
| Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4 | EP16 | 1264.2 | 1447.3 | +14.5% | 276.1 → 273.9 |

| Qwen3 30B-A3B BF16 † | EP8 | 1047.7 | 1316.1 | +25.6% | 264.4 → 267.6 |
| Qwen3 30B-A3B MXFP8 | EP8 | 1521.4 | 1609.5 | +5.8% | 178.5 → 176.5 |
| Qwen3.5-VL 35B BF16 † | EP8 | 708.9 | 848.3 | +19.7% | 221.5 → 223.8 |

- A/A control: GPT-OSS 120B BF16 on `alltoall` in both pipelines differs by −0.4%.

**GB200**

| Benchmark | Parallelism | HybridEP | NCCL EP | Δ | Peak mem (GB) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DeepSeek V3 BF16 †, 256 GPUs | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 885.6 | 905.7 | +2.3% | 161.8 → 163.0 |
| DeepSeek V3 MXFP8, 256 GPUs | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 1265.0 | 1306.9 | +3.3% | 172.8 → 171.3 |
| DeepSeek V3 NVFP4, 256 GPUs | PP4 VP4 EP64 | 1481.9 | 1492.6 | +0.7% | 185.9 → 185.9 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP8, 128 GPUs | EP32 | 733.4 | 750.3 | +2.3% | 184.1 → 183.2 |
| Nemotron 3 Super MXFP8, 64 GPUs | TP2 EP16 | 761.6 | 780.1 | +2.4% | 160.2 → 160.2 |
| Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4, 64 GPUs | TP2 EP16 | 701.1 | 723.3 | +3.2% | 171.5 → 171.1 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning BF16 †, 8 GPUs | EP8 | 785.5 | 823.2 | +4.8% | 168.2 → 172.7 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning MXFP8, 8 GPUs | EP8 | 852.5 | 891.7 | +4.6% | 154.4 → 154.3 |

- In every EP ≤ 32 pair in the tables above, NCCL EP spends less GPU time per dispatch+combine and exposes less communication. Overlapping compute kernels run longer, which gives back part of the saving.
- At EP64 (DeepSeek V3) the gains are smaller. On VRNVL72 BF16, NCCL EP's dispatch+combine takes 25% longer (1,652 vs 1,327 µs) and the gain comes from the grouped-tensor GEMMs. On GB200, every DeepSeek V3 HybridEP run slows by 1.4–2.4% between steps 11–20 and 31–45 while NCCL EP does not, so over steps 11–20 the DeepSeek V3 gains are only +0.2% to +1.1%.
- Peak reserved memory changes by −13.1 to +4.5 GB per GPU. The largest increase on GB200 is +4.5 GB (Lightning BF16).

## Tests

- The new `test_gb200_ncclep_perf_recipes.py` checks the full NCCL EP stack on 12 GB200 recipes (this PR's 10 plus the two Nemotron 3 Ultra recipes from `main`). It also checks that 14 GB200 recipes kept on HybridEP don't pick it up: the four Qwen3 235B-A22B 256-GPU recipes this PR no longer switches, and 10 others, several of which share a base or parent recipe with a switched one.
- `test_gb300_ncclep_perf_recipes.py` now checks the NCCL EP stack on all 29 VRNVL72 NCCL EP recipes: the 27 above plus the two Nemotron 3 Ultra recipes. This replaces its check that the VRNVL72 aliases stay on HybridEP. It also checks that the 16 VRNVL72 MoE recipes left off NCCL EP don't pick it up.
- Existing tests that hardcoded HybridEP for switched recipes are updated:
  - GB200:
    - The Nemotron 3 Super BF16 perf-vs-library test now treats NCCL EP as a benchmark-only difference. The library recipe stays on HybridEP.
    - The Lightning-vs-Nano policy test allows for the dispatcher environment differing between the two.
    - The DeepSeek V4 Flash GB300 test also asserts that GB300 stays on HybridEP.
  - VRNVL72: the full-iteration, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V3 proxy and Qwen3.5-VL workload tests now expect NCCL EP.
  - GB300: the DeepSeek V3 MXFP8 proxy parity test now expects NCCL EP on both 64-GPU proxies.

# Scope

- **GB200:**
  - When this PR was opened, nemo-ci benchmarked 22 GB200 MoE recipes, all on HybridEP. `main` has since moved Nemotron 3 Ultra MXFP8 and NVFP4 to NCCL EP, and this PR switches 10 more.
  - DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP8 is switched without GB300 precedent; #6171 removed its GB300 switch as unverified.
  - Left on HybridEP, although their GB300 counterparts run NCCL EP: Kimi K2 MXFP8, Nemotron 3 Nano BF16/MXFP8, and Qwen3 30B-A3B 8-GPU BF16/MXFP8 and 32-GPU BF16.
  - Qwen3 235B-A22B 256-GPU BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 and MXFP8 large-scale also stay on HybridEP: NCCL EP showed no gain (see [Validation](#validation)). Their GB300 counterparts run NCCL EP.
  - GPT-OSS 120B BF16 stays on `alltoall`, as on GB300.
  - GB200 recipes without a nemo-ci benchmark are not touched.
  - `deepseek_v3_pretrain_256gpu_gb200_fp8mx_partial_cg_dev_config` stays on HybridEP deliberately: it offloads `expert_fc1` with EP overlap, and MCore rejects that combination under `ncclep`.
- **VRNVL72:**
  - Only the tracked benchmarks switch; the rest stay identical to `main`.
  - Some switched recipes have no NCCL EP counterpart on GB200 or GB300: Qwen3 30B-A3B NVFP4, Qwen3.5-VL 35B MXFP8, and Qwen3.5-VL 397B BF16 and MXFP8.
  - DeepSeek V4 Flash ran on NCCL EP on GB200 and VRNVL72 with `nightly-2026-10-16` ([Results](#results)). An earlier GB200 NCCL EP run hit the determinism error below.
  - SM budgets come from the HybridEP recipes. Megatron-Core routes `moe_hybridep_num_sms` to `moe_flex_dispatcher_num_sms`, which NCCL EP uses: 32 SMs for most recipes and 16 for Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.

# DeepSeek determinism setting

- In nemo-ci, DeepSeek V4 Flash GB200 on NCCL EP failed in the first backward pass with TE's `Deterministic execution was requested (NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0 …), but the scale gradient (dprob) is accumulated with nondeterministic atomics` error.
- **Correction to an earlier version of this description: the error is not specific to NCCL EP.**
  - TE raises it in the op-fuser fused grouped MLP (`ops/fused/grouped_mlp.py`) for routed experts whenever `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0` is set and the cuDNN frontend has no deterministic dactivation.
  - Megatron-Core passes the routing probabilities into that MLP the same way for HybridEP and NCCL EP.
  - The check arrived with TE #3407 (2026-09-04), so the recipe's HybridEP golden most likely ran on an older container.
- Any DeepSeek recipe that uses the op fuser and pins `=0` can therefore hit this error on a recent container, whatever its dispatcher. That includes `main`'s GB200 HybridEP DeepSeek V3 MXFP8/NVFP4 recipes. On `main`, the GB300 DeepSeek V3 recipes no longer pin the setting, apart from the dedicated deterministic recipe.
- **This PR keeps `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO` as on `main`: `=0` on the GB200 and VRNVL72 DeepSeek recipes, and `=1` on the GB300 and VRNVL72 64-GPU MXFP8 proxies (#6603)**, so the dispatcher stays the only difference from the HybridEP baselines.
- On a container where TE raises this error, the DeepSeek recipes that use the op-fuser grouped MLP fail in the first backward pass on either dispatcher:
  - GB200: DeepSeek V3 MXFP8, NVFP4 and MXFP8 large-scale, and DeepSeek V4 Flash.
  - VRNVL72: DeepSeek V3 128-GPU MXFP8, 256-GPU MXFP8 and NVFP4, the 64-GPU NVFP4 and 4-GPU MXFP8/NVFP4 proxies, and DeepSeek V4 Flash.
- On VRNVL72, the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning recipe notes that the Rubin image lacks TE #3273 (2026-08-31), which would put it before this check. That is unverified.

# Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- Local CPU unit tests were run with CPU torch and Megatron-Core at `main`'s pin `3914483`, using import-only stubs for Triton and TE.
  - The GB200 and GB300/VRNVL72 NCCL EP tests pass 97/97.
  - Across 23 related test files, 1255 passed and 38 failed:
    - 37 need Hugging Face config downloads, which are blocked locally.
    - `test_known_cross_package_collisions_have_explicit_benchmark_precedence` fails the same way on a clean `main` snapshot.
  - `tests/unit_tests/scripts/performance/test_recipe_environment.py` could not run locally (no `nemo_run`). This PR does not change launcher code.
  - The functional test `test_perf_config_integration.py` was updated but could not run locally, because it also needs HF configs.
- After merging `main` (7623dab, conflict with #6567 in `test_nemotron_3_5_lightning_perf_recipes.py`): `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass and pre-commit passes. The unit tests were not rerun locally after the merges: the local test environment has transformers 4.57, and this branch requires 5.15 or later. GitHub CI runs them.
- The 29 VRNVL72 NCCL EP recipes build offline and pass Megatron-Core's NCCL EP constraints:
  - none uses drop-and-pad;
  - the static-capacity recipes have the op fuser, grouped GEMM and `NVTE_CUTEDSL_FUSED_GROUPED_MLP=1`;
  - none combines A2A overlap with `expert_fc1` offload.
  - Rubin reports compute capability 10.7, which Bridge's NCCL EP hardware check accepts.
- nemo-ci benchmark results are in [Results](#results). These runs used the container's Megatron-LM, not Bridge's pin.
- **Dropped from this PR after measurement on NCCL EP:**
  - GPT-OSS 120B BF16 measured 543.6 vs 581 TFLOP/s/GPU (−6.3%) against its `alltoall` golden.
  - GPT-OSS 120B BF16 on VRNVL72 (switched in 86df0e8, reverted in f61f7da) measured 776.6 vs 887.2 TFLOP/s/GPU (−12.5%) against an `alltoall` run on the same image. NCCL EP passes FP32 routing probabilities, so GPT-OSS's expert-bias add runs in FP32 (+366 ms per iteration); the dispatcher kernels themselves take less GPU time than `alltoall`'s.
  - Qwen3 30B-A3B 8-GPU measured +2.4% (BF16) and +1.9% (MXFP8).
  - Qwen3 235B-A22B on 256 GB200 GPUs measured 793.6 vs 797.0 TFLOP/s/GPU (−0.4%, BF16), 1097.6 vs 1097.2 (+0.0%, MXFP8) and 1217.2 vs 1227.7 (−0.9%, NVFP4) against same-image HybridEP runs. Its MXFP8 large-scale recipe, which builds on the MXFP8 recipe, was not measured and stays on HybridEP too.
